summary: encryptstringadmin fetches and executes obfuscated remote JavaScript on every API call
details: dist/index.js is obfuscator.io-style obfuscated (rotated string array with custom-base64 decoder). Every exported API (loadEncryptString, encryptStringAdmin, decryptStringAdmin, and related helpers) reconstructs a hardcoded CDN URL from the obfuscated string array, fetches JavaScript from that URL with `cache: 'no-store'` and a cache-busting `_esa=<timestamp>` query parameter, and passes the response body directly into `new Function('CryptoJS', <body>)`, then invokes it — the returned closure becomes `impl` and backs every exported function. No hash, signature, or version pin protects the fetched code, and the destination URL is deliberately hidden behind runtime string reconstruction. Any consumer that requires this package and calls any of its APIs executes attacker-controlled JavaScript pulled from an author-mutable endpoint, in the consumer's process, with no ability to audit what will run.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
